name: Sunda Strait
genZNote: When Malacca gets too crowded (or too risky), Sunda is Indonesia's own backup lane — same idea, different island gap.

sections.heading: 🚨 Location & What It Connects
bullets: A strait between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra.
Connects the Java Sea (and the wider Indonesian archipelago/Pacific side) to the Indian Ocean, offering an alternative to the Strait of Malacca further north.
Narrower and shallower than Malacca, which limits it mostly to smaller vessels rather than the largest container ships and tankers.

sections.heading: ⚓ Why It Matters
bullets: A secondary route between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea/Pacific side of Indonesia, used when Malacca is congested or as a shorter option for regional traffic.
Entirely within Indonesian waters, unlike Malacca which is shared among Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore.
Sits near the volcanic island of Krakatoa, historically significant for a major 19th-century eruption.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Sunda Strait, between Java and Sumatra, is a secondary Indonesian route linking the Indian Ocean to the Java Sea, an alternative to the Strait of Malacca.
keyFacts: Connects the Indian Ocean to the Java Sea.
An alternative to the more heavily used Strait of Malacca.
commonConfusion: Sunda Strait is entirely within Indonesia, unlike Malacca which is shared among three countries.

highYieldFacts: Sunda Strait: between Java and Sumatra; Indian Ocean ↔ Java Sea.
Alternative to the Strait of Malacca.
Too shallow/narrow for the largest vessels.
commonTraps: Don't assume Sunda can substitute fully for Malacca — its depth limits it to smaller ships.
mustRemember: Sunda Strait = Indonesia's own Malacca alternative, Java-Sumatra gap.
